structured_output.world_model:
W2 (empirical), after E057. Tip E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535 (seeds 0-2). Rebuilds of the same commit: E049 gave 0.7535 / 0.7552 / 0.7536 across E049, E050 and E057, with time 5.198 / 5.206 / 5.223 s. The E036 tip gave 0.7532 / 0.7525 / 0.7497 / 0.7544 across builds. So the 3-seed mean moves about 0.1-0.3 pp per rebuild and time moves about 0.03 s. E056 (ReLU diagnostic) came in at 4.95 s, so time forecasts have missed on the fast side for variants that cut work (E046, E048, E052, E056).

Mechanisms, each tied to its experiments:
1. Epoch dial: about 1.5-2 s/pp, or about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027, E049).
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded with batch size and an RNG re-draw, E006) are already in the tip. More than 10 time-neutral boosters came out flat or negative (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, and the wd and LS changes). Optimizer, averaging and regularization are flat within about 0.2 pp.
3. Time tracks pixels and steps. Early 20 px is nearly free (E026, E033). Trimming steps or samples costs about the dial's rate (E031, E040, E041, E045, E048).
4. Backward truncation is the best lever (E028, E034, E036, E046, E049, E053). It saves bandwidth-bound BN/GELU and optimizer traffic as well as FLOPs. Freezing the stem before about 75% loses (E037, E054, E055). Group 2 tolerates a freeze from 85-90% (E053 read 0.7562, 5.07 s).
5. Architecture cuts cost accuracy at the dial's rate or worse (E010, E021, E051).
6. Non-step overhead is about 2.5% (E047), so pure systems work saves at most about 1%.
7. Noise: the population mean is about 0.752-0.7535, and headroom over the 0.75 bar is about 0.2 pp. Seed sets used for keeps carry a winner's curse of 0.1-0.2 pp. Candidates cluster around 4.95-5.2 s and 0.752-0.756.

Misses: I over-predicted time on E046, E048, E052 and E056, and under-predicted accuracy on E053.

Unsure:
- The rebuild SD of a 20-seed mean (I guess 0.08 pp).
- Whether E052 or E053 passes a frozen gate. Their population means are likely about 0.7515-0.753.
- Whether coarse labels ship in the train pickle.
- Whether the ReLU time saving is real or build noise.
- Whether the PCIe judge's build matches the local one.

forecasts.reason: Gate with sigma_tot about 0.12 pp needs a mean of about 0.752. E053 or E052 probably passes at the margin. The re-keep ar.py is one build, so the draw is noisy.
E046 is E049 minus 0.25 epoch. The expected dial is about 0.1 s for 0.1 pp, which is lost in rebuild noise. The dial estimate will have a wide error bar.
The standard CIFAR-100 pickle does have coarse_labels, but the benchmark loader likely exposes only fine labels, so this is probably blocked. If it runs, the effect is small.
BatchNorm.__init__ sets weight.requires_grad=False, so the scale is already frozen. The idea closes by code read and the run is a no-op.
The saving is below 0.5%, which is below build noise. Accuracy is likely flat within noise.
This is an offline diagnostic with no recipe change. The curves probably give a loose ordering, and a single threshold is unlikely to separate the cases cleanly.

cruxes: What is the rebuild SD of a 20-seed mean (H4.5.1)? It decides whether any sub-0.15 pp keep decision is real, and whether E052 or E053 (about 5.0-5.07 s) can pass a frozen gate.
Do coarse labels ship in the benchmark's training data? If not, H1.8 closes. I think the loader exposes fine labels only.
Is the E056 ReLU speed gain (about 4.95 s vs 5.2 s) real? If so it is a large lever, and if not it is build noise.
